title: True or False: The Product Owner can change the Definition of Done at any time to adjust to new quality standards. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done is created collaboratively by the Scrum Team and serves as a shared commitment to quality. Any changes must be agreed upon by the entire team to maintain consistency and shared understanding. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed as part of the Increment.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a shared agreement within the team and should not be changed unilaterally by the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done is established by the Scrum Team and changes should involve the entire team.

title: A critical bug is discovered mid-Sprint that impacts the product’s core functionality. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to prioritize and address critical bugs within the current Sprint to maintain product functionality and quality. “Developers are responsible for turning Product Backlog items into Increments of value each Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Wait until the next Sprint to address the bug to maintain the current focus.
explanation1: Incorrect: Critical issues that impact core functionality should be addressed immediately to ensure product integrity.
answer2: Work with the Developers to prioritize the bug fix within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing critical bugs promptly ensures that the product remains functional and reliable.
answer3: Delay the fix until it can be scheduled in a future Sprint to avoid disrupting the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying critical fixes compromises product quality and stakeholder trust.
answer4: Escalate the bug to management for immediate intervention.
explanation4: Incorrect: Critical issues should be managed by the Scrum Team without external escalation unless absolutely necessary.

title: The Product Owner notices that several Product Backlog items are consistently not meeting the Definition of Done. What should be their first step? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the team to understand why items are not meeting the Definition of Done, helping to identify areas for improvement in processes or standards. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Lower the standards of the Definition of Done to accommodate the team’s capabilities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards compromises the product and is not a viable solution.
answer2: Collaborate with the team to identify why the Definition of Done is not being met.
explanation2: Correct: Working together to identify and address issues ensures that the Definition of Done is achievable and maintained.
answer3: Remove unfinished items from the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: Removing items without addressing the root cause does not solve the underlying problem.
answer4: Delay all items not meeting the Definition of Done to the next Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Delaying items without addressing why they did not meet the Definition of Done does not ensure improvement.

title: Which two actions are recommended if the team consistently misses the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Reviewing the Definition of Done and focusing on testing and quality throughout the Sprint help the Scrum Team consistently meet their quality standards. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Review and adjust the Definition of Done during the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation1: Correct: Reviewing and adjusting the Definition of Done ensures it remains realistic and achievable while maintaining quality.
answer2: Increase the focus on testing and quality assurance throughout the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Emphasizing quality throughout the Sprint helps the team meet the Definition of Done consistently.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to enforce stricter quality controls.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Team as a whole is responsible for quality, not just the Scrum Master.
answer4: Skip less critical tasks to ensure critical tasks meet the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Incorrect: Skipping tasks compromises the Sprint Goal and overall Sprint integrity.
answer5: Extend the Sprint length to ensure all criteria are met.
explanation5: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint violates Scrum’s principles and undermines the team’s time-box commitment.

title: Which three key elements help ensure the quality and consistency of the work done by a Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Definition of Done, Sprint Retrospective, and Backlog Refinement are critical to maintaining high-quality work by setting clear standards and continuously improving the team's processes. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Scrum Artifacts
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done sets clear criteria for when work is considered complete, ensuring quality standards.
answer2: Sprint Retrospective
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective helps the team identify areas for improvement, maintaining consistency and quality.
answer3: Backlog Refinement
explanation3: Correct: Refining the Product Backlog ensures that the team fully understands what needs to be done, reducing ambiguity and maintaining quality.
answer4: Daily Scrum
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Daily Scrum helps track progress, it does not directly ensure quality and consistency.
answer5: Sprint Review
explanation5: Incorrect: The Sprint Review gathers feedback but does not directly establish quality criteria.

title: During a Daily Scrum, the Developers identify a potential improvement to their approach. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should encourage the Developers to explore improvements that help achieve the Sprint Goal, supporting their autonomy and focus on value. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the discussion as it is outside the Product Owner's responsibilities.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner should stay engaged and understand how changes might impact value delivery.
answer2: Encourage the team to explore the improvement if it helps achieve the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should support improvements that align with the Sprint Goal and maximize value.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to ensure the team does not change their approach mid-Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should be empowered to adapt their plan to best achieve the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Direct the team to stick to the original plan to avoid risks.
explanation4: Incorrect: Flexibility is key in adapting to better ways of working during the Sprint.

title: The Scrum Master notices that the team is not using the Daily Scrum effectively. What is the best action for the Scrum Master to take? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the team on how to use the Daily Scrum effectively, helping them to inspect progress and adapt their plans. “The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and that attendees understand its purpose.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Dictate how the Daily Scrum should be conducted to ensure it's effective.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not control the Daily Scrum.
answer2: Coach the team on how to use the Daily Scrum to inspect and adapt their progress towards the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should guide the team in optimizing the Daily Scrum to support their self-management.
answer3: Ignore the issue to avoid disrupting the team’s autonomy.
explanation3: Incorrect: Coaching on effective practices is part of the Scrum Master’s role.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to set the agenda for the Daily Scrum.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers, and the Product Owner does not control it.

title: True or False: The Product Backlog must be fully refined before the start of each Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing process where items are continuously refined and detailed as needed, rather than being fully refined before each Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is continuously refined; not all items need to be fully detailed before each Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity that continues throughout the Sprint.

title: True or False: The Product Owner should always adjust the Product Backlog immediately when receiving new feedback. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate new feedback and adjust the Product Backlog thoughtfully to ensure it aligns with the overall product strategy and value delivery. “The Product Owner is responsible for effective Product Backlog management, including ensuring that the Product Backlog is transparent, visible, and understood.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Immediate adjustments without careful consideration can disrupt the strategic direction of the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should assess feedback carefully and make thoughtful adjustments to the Product Backlog when appropriate.

title: Which two strategies should the Product Owner use to maximize the value of the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Maximizing value involves prioritizing items that deliver the highest business impact and continuously updating the Backlog based on feedback and market changes. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Order Backlog items based on technical feasibility alone.
explanation1: Incorrect: Prioritization should focus on value delivery, not just technical aspects.
answer2: Prioritize items that deliver the highest business value first.
explanation2: Correct: Ordering items by business value ensures the most impactful work is completed first.
answer3: Regularly incorporate feedback from stakeholders and the market.
explanation3: Correct: Incorporating feedback ensures the Product Backlog remains relevant and aligned with external needs.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback that does not align with current priorities.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to maintain a responsive and adaptable Backlog.
answer5: Delegate prioritization to Developers to speed up decision-making.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing the Product Backlog based on value delivery.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when the Product Backlog is too large to manage effectively? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders to prioritize the Backlog and refine it into smaller, actionable items, ensuring it remains manageable and focused on value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Remove low-priority items to streamline the Backlog without consulting stakeholders.
explanation1: Incorrect: Removing items arbitrarily without input can reduce value and misalign with stakeholder needs.
answer2: Collaborate with stakeholders to reprioritize and refine the Backlog, focusing on high-value items.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborating with stakeholders ensures the Backlog reflects the most current and valuable priorities.
answer3: Break down large items into smaller, manageable pieces to make the Backlog more actionable.
explanation3: Correct: Decomposing large items makes the Backlog more manageable and helps the team deliver value incrementally.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to take over managing the Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for Backlog management and cannot delegate this responsibility.
answer5: Delay refinement until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement should be an ongoing process, not delayed until formal planning.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to keep the Product Backlog aligned with current market trends? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders regularly and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with market needs and maximize value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Update the Product Backlog only during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously refined and updated based on new insights.
answer2: Engage regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement ensures the Product Backlog stays relevant and aligned with market conditions.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-impact items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help keep the Product Backlog focused on delivering the most value.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to maintain the Backlog’s current structure.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Backlog adaptable and responsive.
answer5: Delegate Backlog refinement to the Developers to save time.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: Which three strategies best demonstrate the Product Owner’s role in maximizing the value of the product? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes product value by continuously engaging stakeholders, using data-driven prioritization, and maintaining a well-refined Product Backlog that guides the team’s efforts. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Allowing the Scrum Master to make prioritization decisions for the Product Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for Backlog prioritization and value delivery.
answer2: Regularly engaging stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures the Product Backlog reflects the latest needs and value opportunities.
answer3: Using data and metrics to inform prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help align work with business goals and value.
answer4: Ensuring Backlog items are refined and ready for future Sprints.
explanation4: Correct: Well-refined Backlog items help the team deliver consistent, incremental value.
answer5: Focusing only on technical improvements without considering business impact.
explanation5: Incorrect: Prioritization should consider both business and technical factors to maximize value.

title: What are the two main reasons the Product Owner might adjust the order of the Product Backlog during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner adjusts the Product Backlog to respond to changes in the market and to feedback, ensuring the product remains valuable. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: To address urgent market changes.
explanation1: Correct: Market changes can influence the priority of Product Backlog items.
answer2: To ensure all items can be completed within the Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Items in the Product Backlog are not adjusted based on Sprint completion.
answer3: To respond to stakeholder feedback received during the Sprint.
explanation3: Correct: Feedback can prompt adjustments to maintain the product's value.
answer4: To improve team efficiency.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is ordered for value delivery, not solely for team efficiency.
answer5: To align with changes in team capacity.
explanation5: Incorrect: Team capacity is not a reason to reorder the Product Backlog during a Sprint.

title: A key stakeholder requests an urgent change during the Sprint. What is the most appropriate action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate the new request, prioritize it within the Product Backlog, and manage stakeholder expectations without disrupting the current Sprint. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Add the change to the current Sprint to keep stakeholders happy.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding new work during a Sprint disrupts the team's focus and the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the request and prioritize it in the Product Backlog for future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage new requests through the Product Backlog, ensuring alignment with priorities.
answer3: Reject the request outright to maintain the current Sprint scope.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner should consider all feedback, even if it cannot be actioned immediately.
answer4: Ask the team to work extra hours to accommodate the change.
explanation4: Incorrect: Overworking the team is not sustainable and contradicts Scrum principles.

title: During a Sprint, the team discovers that a feature being developed is no longer aligned with the current market needs. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with the team and stakeholders to reassess priorities when market needs change, ensuring the work remains aligned with the highest value. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue with the feature as planned to avoid disrupting the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Continuing with a misaligned feature does not deliver value and can waste resources.
answer2: Discuss with the team and stakeholders to reassess the feature's priority.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should reassess priorities to ensure the team is always working on the most valuable items.
answer3: Cancel the Sprint and restart with a new focus.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling a Sprint is an extreme measure and should be used only when absolutely necessary.
answer4: Remove the feature from the Sprint Backlog immediately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Changes to the Sprint Backlog should be carefully managed and not done impulsively.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team highlights repeated challenges with unclear requirements for Product Backlog items. How should the Product Owner respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage in refining Backlog items with the team, ensuring clarity and understanding to enhance future Sprint success. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback to avoid changing current processes.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback prevents improvement and does not address recurring issues.
answer2: Work with the team to improve the refinement process, ensuring requirements are clear and well understood.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement processes helps ensure that Backlog items are actionable and reduce misunderstandings.
answer3: Delegate the responsibility of clarifying requirements to the Scrum Master.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and must actively participate in clarifying requirements.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next formal refinement session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be addressed continuously, not delayed.

title: True or False: The Product Owner can delegate the responsibility of managing stakeholder engagement to the Scrum Master. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for engaging stakeholders and managing their expectations, ensuring the product reflects their needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for stakeholder engagement and cannot delegate this responsibility.
explanation2: Correct: Managing stakeholder engagement is a key responsibility of the Product Owner, who must actively ensure alignment.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is solely responsible for the content and ordering of the Product Backlog. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is fully accountable for managing the Product Backlog, ensuring it reflects the highest value work at all times. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, including its content and prioritization.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s role includes managing and prioritizing the Product Backlog to maximize value.

title: Which two roles are directly involved in maintaining and prioritizing the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner and Development Team work together to ensure the Product Backlog is clear, prioritized, and ready for future Sprints. “The Product Owner is accountable for ensuring that the Product Backlog is understood.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Scrum Master
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner prioritizes, while the Scrum Master facilitates; only the Product Owner manages the Backlog.
answer2: Product Owner
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner manages prioritization, and the Development Team collaborates on understanding and refining items.
answer3: Development Team
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner manages prioritization, and the Development Team collaborates on understanding and refining items.
answer4: Manager
explanation4: Incorrect: Manager isn't a scrum role
answer5: Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide input, but prioritization and refinement are primarily the responsibilities of the Product Owner and Development Team.

title: Which three key responsibilities does the Product Owner have in Scrum? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing the Product Backlog, engaging stakeholders, and collaboratively defining the Sprint Goal with the Scrum Team. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Prioritizing Product Backlog items based on value and feedback.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner ensures that the most valuable and impactful items are prioritized.
answer2: Engaging with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Ongoing stakeholder engagement ensures the Product Backlog reflects current needs and maximizes product value.
answer3: Defining the Sprint Goal in collaboration with the Scrum Team.
explanation3: Correct: The Sprint Goal is set in collaboration to align the team’s efforts with the Product Backlog priorities.
answer4: Assigning tasks to the Development Team during Sprint Planning.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Development Team is self-organizing and selects their own tasks based on the Sprint Goal.
answer5: Approving the Increment before the Sprint Review.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Increment is inspected collectively during the Sprint Review, not pre-approved by the Product Owner.

title: Which two actions are essential for the Product Owner to maximize the value of the product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes product value by clearly defining Backlog items and actively collaborating with stakeholders to refine and prioritize work. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Clearly defining Product Backlog items.
explanation1: Correct: Clearly defined Product Backlog items help the team understand what is needed, ensuring the product delivers value.
answer2: Regularly collaborating with stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborating with stakeholders helps the Product Owner gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog to maximize value.
answer3: Assigning tasks to the Development Team.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Development Team is self-organizing and assigns their own tasks.
answer4: Facilitating all Scrum events to ensure they run smoothly.
explanation4: Incorrect: Facilitating events is primarily the responsibility of the Scrum Master, not the Product Owner.
answer5: Maintaining the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: The entire Scrum Team maintains the Definition of Done, not just the Product Owner.

title: The Product Owner has requested that the team work on an urgent task outside the current Sprint Goal. How should the team handle this request? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The team should discuss urgent tasks with the Product Owner and reprioritize them in the Product Backlog, addressing them in the next Sprint Planning session. “During the Sprint, scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Add the task to the current Sprint to accommodate the request.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding unplanned tasks disrupts focus and the team’s commitment to the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Discuss the urgency and prioritize the task in the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should adjust the Product Backlog, and the team can address it in future planning sessions.
answer3: Ignore the request to maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring the Product Owner’s request without discussion is not collaborative.
answer4: Reassign existing tasks to make room for the urgent task.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reassigning tasks without proper planning can undermine the team’s workflow and focus.

title: A Product Owner finds that the Developers are not completing items as planned. What should the Product Owner do first? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to understand and resolve any impediments impacting their progress. This approach fosters a supportive and problem-solving environment. “The Scrum Team is responsible for all product-related activities.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately escalate the issue to management.
explanation1: Incorrect: Issues should first be addressed within the Scrum Team.
answer2: Work with the Developers to identify any impediments affecting progress.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborating with the Developers to identify and address impediments is the most effective first step.
answer3: Reassign the incomplete work to another team.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reassigning work disrupts team dynamics and focus.
answer4: Adjust the Product Backlog priorities immediately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjusting priorities may not address the root cause of the issue.

title: True or False: The Increment is an artifact that provides transparency into the work completed during the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment provides transparency by showing completed work at the end of the Sprint, making it available for inspection and adaptation. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Increment provides a clear view of what has been completed and is ready for inspection.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Increment is specifically designed to offer transparency into completed work.

title: Which three aspects are crucial to maintaining a transparent Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining a transparent Product Backlog requires regular updates, clear item descriptions, and frequent refinement sessions to keep everyone aligned. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly updating items based on stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Correct: Regular updates ensure that the Product Backlog reflects current priorities and stakeholder needs.
answer2: Clear and concise descriptions for each Product Backlog item.
explanation2: Correct: Well-defined items help the team understand what needs to be done, promoting clarity and focus.
answer3: The Product Owner’s exclusive control over prioritization.
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Product Owner prioritizes, transparency involves clear communication with the team and stakeholders.
answer4: Detailed estimates for all items at all times.
explanation4: Incorrect: Detailed estimates are useful, but transparency is about clear communication, not constant detailed estimates.
answer5: Frequent refinement sessions involving the whole Scrum Team.
explanation5: Correct: Refinement sessions help ensure that the Product Backlog is well understood and ready for upcoming Sprints.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when the team struggles to meet the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to improve refinement practices, ensuring that Backlog items meet the Definition of Done and maintaining quality standards. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the issue to maintain the Sprint’s pace.
explanation1: Incorrect: Failing to meet the Definition of Done compromises quality and consistency.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to identify obstacles and improve refinement practices.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration helps address obstacles and ensures items meet the Definition of Done consistently.
answer3: Lower the Definition of Done temporarily to make items easier to complete.
explanation3: Incorrect: Lowering standards undermines product quality and value.
answer4: Facilitate additional refinement sessions to enhance item clarity.
explanation4: Correct: Improving refinement helps ensure that items are clear, manageable, and meet the Definition of Done.
answer5: Assign the Scrum Master to enforce adherence to the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: Adherence to the Definition of Done is a shared responsibility of the Scrum Team.

title: During Backlog Refinement, the Development Team encounters a highly complex item that they do not fully understand. What is the best next step? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: When an item is not well understood, the Development Team should seek clarification from the Product Owner to ensure accurate estimation and planning. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Proceed with estimating the item despite the uncertainty.
explanation1: Incorrect: Estimating without understanding increases risk and may result in poor planning and unexpected challenges.
answer2: Seek clarification from the Product Owner and adjust the item as needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for clarifying items, ensuring the team fully understands the requirements before estimating.
answer3: Defer the item to the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation3: Incorrect: Deferment without understanding delays planning and may impact future Sprints.
answer4: Split the item into smaller parts immediately without further discussion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Splitting without clarification can lead to incomplete or incorrect work breakdown.

title: Which artifact directly supports Inspection by providing a tangible output of work completed during the Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment supports Inspection by providing a concrete output of completed work that can be reviewed and assessed. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog outlines future work but does not provide a tangible output.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment represents completed work and is inspected during the Sprint Review.
answer3: Sprint Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows planned work but does not provide an output for inspection.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not produce a tangible output.

title: Which artifact provides visibility into the work completed and helps the team track progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment shows completed work and serves as a stepping stone toward achieving the Product Goal, demonstrating progress to the team and stakeholders. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows the plan for the current Sprint but does not track progress toward the Product Goal.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment represents the current state of work completed, providing visibility into progress toward the Product Goal.
answer3: Product Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists future work and priorities but does not directly show completed progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not provide a view of completed work.

title: True or False: The Development Team must complete all tasks in the Sprint Backlog to achieve the Sprint Goal. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Achieving the Sprint Goal does not necessarily require completing all tasks in the Sprint Backlog; the focus is on meeting the objectives set by the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint, though not all Sprint Backlog items have to be completed for the Sprint Goal to be met.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is the target of the Sprint, and some tasks may not need completion if the goal is met through other means.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal can be achieved even if some tasks are not completed, as long as the key objectives are met.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must attend every Sprint Retrospective to assess the Developers’ performance. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Retrospective is a collaborative event focused on improving processes and teamwork, not monitoring individual performance. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Retrospective focuses on process improvement, not evaluating individual performance.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner participates in the Retrospective to contribute to team improvements, not to assess performance.

title: Which three elements are critical for a successful Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: A successful Sprint Retrospective requires a safe environment, actionable improvements, and full participation from the Scrum Team, fostering continuous improvement. “The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint by planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: A safe environment where team members feel comfortable sharing their thoughts.
explanation1: Correct: A safe environment encourages open and honest feedback, crucial for identifying improvements.
answer2: A focus on identifying actionable improvements for the next Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective aims to identify and plan specific changes to improve the team’s process and performance.
answer3: Active participation from the entire Scrum Team, including the Product Owner.
explanation3: Correct: The entire Scrum Team’s participation ensures diverse perspectives and collective ownership of improvements.
answer4: Detailed discussions on task assignments for the next Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Task assignments are part of Sprint Planning, not the Retrospective.
answer5: Approval of improvement actions by management before implementation.
explanation5: Incorrect: Improvements are decided and implemented by the Scrum Team; external approval is not required.

title: Which two events in Scrum provide opportunities to inspect and adapt the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Review and Backlog Refinement provide formal opportunities to inspect and adapt the Product Backlog, ensuring it remains relevant and valuable. “Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity to add details, such as a description, order, and size.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Review
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Review allows inspection of the Increment, and Backlog Refinement prepares items for future Sprints.
answer2: Sprint Planning
explanation2: Incorrect: Sprint Planning sets up the Sprint, and the Daily Scrum inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal, not the Backlog.
answer3: Sprint Retrospective
explanation3: Incorrect: The Retrospective focuses on process improvement, and the Definition of Done is a quality standard, not a Backlog event.
answer4: Daily Scrum
explanation4: Incorrect: Daily Scrum inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal, not the Backlog.
answer5: Backlog Refinement
explanation5: Correct : Backlog Refinement provide formal opportunities to inspect and adapt the Product Backlog

title: What is the main reason a Product Owner should be present at the Sprint Review? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is a key opportunity for the Product Owner to gather feedback from stakeholders and adjust the Product Backlog. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: To approve or reject the completed work.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is not a formal approval session.
answer2: To gather feedback from stakeholders to adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The main purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog based on feedback.
answer3: To present the Product Increment to senior management.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner collaborates with stakeholders, not just senior management.
answer4: To ensure the team met the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: The focus is on gathering feedback rather than just reviewing goals.

title: The Development Team frequently finds that they are working on tasks that are not directly contributing to the Sprint Goal. What is the best way to address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Using the Daily Scrum to discuss and adjust task alignment helps the team stay focused on achieving the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue with the current tasks and complete them as planned.
explanation1: Incorrect: Continuing work that does not support the Sprint Goal detracts from the team’s focus and effectiveness.
answer2: Discuss task alignment during the Daily Scrum and adjust as necessary.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum allows the team to inspect their progress and realign their tasks with the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Reassign tasks to team members who are less busy.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reassigning tasks disrupts self-organization and does not ensure alignment with the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Escalate the issue to the Scrum Master for resolution.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Development Team is responsible for managing their work and ensuring alignment with the Sprint Goal.

title: The team is frequently completing Increments that do not meet the stakeholders’ expectations. Which Scrum event should be used to address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review allows the team to present completed work to stakeholders, gather feedback, and align future efforts with expectations. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Planning
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint Planning sets the goal and scope but does not directly address stakeholder feedback.
answer2: Sprint Review
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review is designed to gather feedback from stakeholders and adjust future work based on their input.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum inspects progress but does not directly involve stakeholders.
answer4: Sprint Retrospective
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective focuses on improving the team’s processes, not product feedback.

title: Which pillar of Scrum encourages the team to make necessary changes immediately when new information is discovered? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Adaptation encourages the team to make changes immediately when new information is discovered, ensuring that they remain aligned with their goals. “Adaptation becomes more difficult when the people involved are not empowered.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Incorrect: Inspection is the process of assessing the situation; Adaptation is the pillar that encourages change.
answer2: Adaptation
explanation2: Correct: Adaptation involves making necessary adjustments as soon as new information is identified.
answer3: Transparency
explanation3: Incorrect: Transparency ensures information is visible but does not directly drive change.
answer4: Courage
explanation4: Incorrect: Courage is a value that supports taking action, but Adaptation specifically involves making changes.

title: Which three pillars of Scrum are demonstrated when the Scrum Team inspects their work and adapts based on their findings? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The pillars of Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation enable the team to continuously improve their processes and outcomes, driving effective Scrum practice. “Scrum relies on three pillars: transparency, inspection, and adaptation.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Correct: Inspection helps the team identify areas for improvement during events like Sprint Reviews and Retrospectives.
answer2: Transparency
explanation2: Correct: Transparency allows the team to openly share progress, challenges, and insights with each other and stakeholders.
answer3: Focus
explanation3: Incorrect: Focus is a value, not a pillar that supports continuous improvement.
answer4: Adaptation
explanation4: Correct: Adaptation enables the team to adjust their work processes based on what was inspected.
answer5: Respect
explanation5: Incorrect: Respect is a value that fosters collaboration but is not one of the three pillars.

title: Which three techniques can the Development Team use to improve their estimation accuracy? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Using Velocity Tracking, conducting Refinement, and applying relative estimation techniques help the Development Team improve estimation accuracy, leading to more achievable Sprints. “The Development Team tracks this total work remaining at least for every Daily Scrum.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Using Velocity Tracking to understand past performance.
explanation1: Correct: Velocity Tracking helps the team gauge their capacity based on past work, improving estimation accuracy.
answer2: Conducting Backlog Refinement to clarify requirements before estimation.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement ensures the team fully understands the work, leading to more accurate estimates.
answer3: Applying relative estimation techniques like Planning Poker.
explanation3: Correct: Techniques like Planning Poker foster discussion and help the team reach a consensus on effort estimates.
answer4: Assigning fixed time frames for each task regardless of complexity.
explanation4: Incorrect: Fixed time frames do not account for variability in task complexity and can lead to inaccurate estimates.
answer5: Skipping estimation to save time for development.
explanation5: Incorrect: Skipping estimation increases the risk of over-commitment and unrealistic planning.

title: Which two tools or techniques can help the Scrum Team ensure that Product Backlog items are well understood before being pulled into a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Backlog Refinement and Definition of Ready help ensure that Product Backlog items are well defined and meet necessary criteria before being selected for a Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing process of keeping the backlog items in good order.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Backlog Refinement
explanation1: Correct: These tool ensure that items are clear and meet criteria before being pulled into the Sprint Backlog.
answer2: Definition of Ready
explanation2: Correct: These tool ensure that items are clear and meet criteria before being pulled into the Sprint Backlog.
answer3: Sprint Review
explanation3: Incorrect: These event focus on completed work, not readiness of future tasks.
answer4: User Story Mapping
explanation4: Incorrect: User Story Mapping helps organize stories, but not ensure readiness.
answer5: Burndown Chart
explanation5: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress, not readiness.

title: During a Sprint Review, the stakeholders express confusion about what was completed versus what was planned. Which tool can help clarify this during future Sprints? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Burndown Chart provides stakeholders with a clear view of what was planned and what was completed during the Sprint, enhancing transparency. “The Sprint Burndown Chart shows the amount of work remaining.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Definition of Ready
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Ready ensures tasks are prepared but does not track planned vs. completed work.
answer2: Sprint Burndown Chart
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Burndown Chart provides a clear visual representation of planned versus completed work, helping stakeholders understand progress.
answer3: Velocity Tracking
explanation3: Incorrect: Velocity measures past performance but does not compare planned versus completed work in real-time.
answer4: Daily Scrum
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum helps track progress internally but does not visually present planned vs. completed work to stakeholders.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team struggles to estimate the effort required for some complex tasks. What technique could they use to improve their estimations? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Planning Poker helps the team estimate complex tasks by fostering discussion and consensus on effort, making it easier to plan effectively for the Sprint. “Scrum Teams may choose their preferred method of estimation.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: User Story Mapping
explanation1: Incorrect: User Story Mapping helps organize and prioritize stories but is not primarily used for estimation.
answer2: Planning Poker
explanation2: Correct: Planning Poker is an estimation technique that encourages team discussion and consensus on task complexity.
answer3: Sprint Retrospective
explanation3: Incorrect: The Retrospective is for reflecting on the past Sprint, not for estimating effort.
answer4: Burndown Chart
explanation4: Incorrect: Burndown Charts track progress but do not assist in estimation.

title: The Product Owner notices that the team’s velocity has decreased over the last three Sprints. What is the best course of action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the team to identify factors affecting velocity and make necessary adjustments to the Product Backlog. “The Scrum Team inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapts the Sprint Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Push the team to increase their output in the next Sprint to match previous velocities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Pushing the team without understanding the cause can lead to burnout and reduced quality.
answer2: Collaborate with the team to identify any impediments and adjust the Product Backlog as needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should work with the team to identify issues and refine the Backlog to better align with team capacity.
answer3: Ignore the issue as velocity is not an indicator of team performance.
explanation3: Incorrect: A decreasing velocity may indicate underlying issues that need to be addressed.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to enforce stricter adherence to the planned work.
explanation4: Incorrect: The team should self-manage and adapt their workload based on their capacity and challenges.

title: The team struggles with consistent communication of task progress, leading to misunderstandings. What tool can best improve this situation? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: A Task Board helps improve communication by providing a visual status of tasks, making it easier for team members to stay aligned and informed. “Task Boards can enhance transparency and provide clear insights into progress.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Backlog Refinement
explanation1: Incorrect: Refinement improves future work readiness but does not enhance daily communication.
answer2: Task Board
explanation2: Correct: A Task Board provides a clear visual status of all tasks, improving communication among team members.
answer3: Scrum Artifacts
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not directly address task communication.
answer4: Sprint Retrospective
explanation4: Incorrect: Retrospectives identify improvements but do not directly enhance task status communication.

title: Which Scrum value is most emphasized when the team commits to a Sprint Goal and works together to achieve it? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Commitment drives the team’s dedication to achieving the Sprint Goal, fostering a unified effort toward completing their objectives. “Scrum’s success is based on people becoming more proficient in living five values.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Courage
explanation1: Incorrect: Courage supports taking bold actions, but Commitment specifically drives dedication to the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Commitment
explanation2: Correct: Commitment emphasizes the team’s dedication to achieving the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Respect
explanation3: Incorrect: Respect fosters positive collaboration, but Commitment is key to pursuing the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Focus
explanation4: Incorrect: Focus helps maintain direction, but Commitment directly relates to achieving the goal.

title: True or False: The Developers are solely responsible for defining the Sprint Goal. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal is a shared objective that is defined by the entire Scrum Team during Sprint Planning, ensuring alignment and commitment. “The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is defined collaboratively by the entire Scrum Team, including the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal is established through collaboration between the Product Owner and the Developers.

title: True or False: The Product Owner should cancel the Sprint if the Developers identify an issue that makes the Sprint Goal unattainable. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner can cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but this action is not mandatory and should be carefully considered. “A Sprint can be canceled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is a decision that should be made carefully, considering all factors, not just the immediate issue.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner may cancel the Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but it is not mandatory.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers realize they need more time to complete a critical Product Backlog item. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the team can complete the most valuable work while maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Extend the Sprint to give the team more time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint durations are fixed and should not be extended under any circumstances.
answer2: Work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog while keeping the Sprint Goal in focus.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog ensures the team remains focused on delivering the most valuable work.
answer3: Delay the item to the next Sprint to ensure it is fully completed.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying critical work should be avoided if it impacts the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Reassign the work to another team to meet the deadline.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reassigning work disrupts the team’s accountability and focus.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers express uncertainty about the effort required for a Backlog item. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine the unclear item, ensuring it is actionable and ready for the Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Insist the item be included to meet stakeholder expectations.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including unclear items can disrupt the Sprint and jeopardize the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item, providing clarity and reducing uncertainty.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement helps ensure that Backlog items are well understood and ready for selection.
answer3: Delay the item until the next Sprint to avoid disruption.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying work without addressing refinement does not solve the underlying problem.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to facilitate additional refinement sessions.
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master can facilitate, the Product Owner leads refinement in collaboration with the Developers.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner learns that the team will not meet the Sprint Goal due to unforeseen technical challenges. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog while maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal. This approach aligns with the principle that scope may be renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned. “The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Push the team to work extra hours to meet the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: Pushing the team to work extra hours contradicts the principles of sustainable pace.
answer2: Work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog while keeping the Sprint Goal in mind.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps refocus efforts without changing the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Cancel the Sprint and start a new one to address the challenges.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is extreme and should only happen if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
answer4: Ignore the issue and continue with the current plan.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring challenges leads to unmet goals and decreased team morale.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers raise concerns about the feasibility of completing the Sprint Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the team commits to achievable work that aligns with the Sprint Goal. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Insist that the team commit to the Sprint Goal regardless of the challenges.
explanation1: Incorrect: Committing to unrealistic goals can lead to burnout and unmet Sprint outcomes.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on the most valuable work.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps align the team’s efforts with achievable, high-value outcomes.
answer3: Delay the Sprint to reevaluate the Sprint Goal and items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying the Sprint disrupts the cadence and flow of work in Scrum.
answer4: Reassign some work to another team to meet the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reassigning work undermines team accountability and focus.

title: During Sprint Review, the stakeholders express that the Increment does not meet their expectations. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog, ensuring alignment with expectations. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the Increment and explain the challenges faced by the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending the work does not address stakeholder concerns or improve the product.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should actively manage stakeholder feedback and refine the Product Backlog based on their input.
answer3: Ignore the feedback and continue with the current plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of the Sprint Review and stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the feedback separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder feedback and expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders express that the Increment does not meet their needs. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage with stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and update the Product Backlog, ensuring future work aligns with their needs. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the Increment by explaining the challenges faced by the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending work without addressing feedback does not improve future iterations.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should actively manage feedback and refine the Backlog to better align with stakeholder needs.
answer3: Ignore the feedback and continue with the planned Backlog items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of the Sprint Review and stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the stakeholder feedback separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder feedback and expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During a Sprint, the Product Owner receives feedback that a key feature is not meeting stakeholder expectations. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate feedback and adjust the Product Backlog to ensure future work aligns with stakeholder needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback to avoid disrupting the current Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can lead to a product that does not meet stakeholder needs.
answer2: Evaluate the feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly for future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Product Backlog ensures that feedback is addressed in future work without disrupting the current Sprint.
answer3: Request the team to rework the feature immediately within the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Mid-Sprint changes disrupt focus and the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the stakeholder feedback.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing stakeholder feedback and refining the Product Backlog.

title: Which three actions demonstrate effective engagement of stakeholders by the Product Owner? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders regularly, use feedback to inform prioritization, and communicate changes clearly to maintain alignment and trust. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only communicating with stakeholders during formal Scrum events.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ongoing communication with stakeholders is crucial for managing expectations and aligning the Product Backlog.
answer2: Engaging stakeholders regularly to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement ensures the Product Backlog remains aligned with stakeholder needs.
answer3: Using stakeholder feedback to guide prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Feedback-driven prioritization helps maximize value and address current needs.
answer4: Clearly communicating the impact of changes to stakeholders.
explanation4: Correct: Transparent communication helps stakeholders understand how their feedback influences the Product Backlog.
answer5: Delegating stakeholder management to the Scrum Master to avoid disruptions.
explanation5: Incorrect: Managing stakeholders is a key responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers identify a potential impediment that could delay their progress. How should the Product Owner respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should support the Developers in addressing impediments, ensuring that progress towards the Sprint Goal is maintained. “The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by removing impediments to the team’s progress.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the impediment to maintain the current focus on the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring impediments can lead to delays and reduce the team’s ability to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Support the Developers in addressing the impediment, ensuring it does not impact progress.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should support the team in maintaining focus on value delivery, though resolving technical impediments is primarily the Developers' responsibility.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to solve the issue independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master facilitates removal of impediments, the Product Owner should stay engaged to understand the impact on value.
answer4: Escalate the issue to management to ensure it is quickly resolved.
explanation4: Incorrect: Escalating issues externally can disrupt the team’s flow and self-management.

title: Which concept is crucial for ensuring that Scrum Teams can adapt quickly to changes and deliver value incrementally? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Inspection and Adaptation are fundamental to Scrum, allowing teams to continuously evaluate and refine their approach, delivering value incrementally. “Scrum relies on transparency, inspection, and adaptation.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Timeboxing
explanation1: Incorrect: Timeboxing limits the duration of Scrum events but does not directly address adaptability.
answer2: Inspection and Adaptation
explanation2: Correct: Inspection and Adaptation allow Scrum Teams to regularly assess their progress and adjust their approach to maximize value.
answer3: Sprint Planning
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprint Planning sets the goal and plan for the Sprint but does not directly ensure adaptability.
answer4: Definition of Ready
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Ready ensures that items are prepared for the Sprint but does not ensure team adaptability.

title: During a Sprint, a key stakeholder requests a major change to the Product Backlog. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner must balance stakeholder needs with the team's current work, managing changes to the Product Backlog as needed. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately add the change to the Sprint Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes during the Sprint should be managed carefully to avoid disrupting the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Discuss the change with the stakeholder and prioritize it in the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should assess the change and adjust the Backlog accordingly, without disrupting the current Sprint.
answer3: Reject the change as it was not planned during the Sprint Planning.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner should not outright reject changes but consider them appropriately.
answer4: Bring the change to the Daily Scrum for discussion with the Developers.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is not intended for discussing backlog changes.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies frequent misunderstandings of Product Backlog items as a significant issue. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively work with the Developers to refine unclear items, ensuring that Product Backlog items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and continue with the current refinement process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can lead to recurring misunderstandings and inefficiencies.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to improve refinement, ensuring items are clear and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement processes ensures items are well understood and reduces misunderstandings in future Sprints.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to handle refinement challenges independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and should be actively involved.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be made continuously, not delayed until planning sessions.

title: During a Sprint Review, stakeholders request additional features based on the latest market trends. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should assess stakeholder feedback and adjust the Product Backlog, prioritizing new features based on their value and impact. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately add the features to the current Sprint Backlog to keep stakeholders satisfied.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog should not be altered during a Sprint; new requests are managed through the Product Backlog.
answer2: Evaluate the request and update the Product Backlog to prioritize the new features accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage stakeholder feedback through the Product Backlog, ensuring alignment with priorities.
answer3: Reject the requests to maintain the current focus of the team.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered and evaluated, even if not immediately actionable.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to communicate to stakeholders that changes are not allowed.
explanation4: Incorrect: Communicating about changes is part of the Product Owner's responsibilities, not the Scrum Master's.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner realizes that the team is falling behind on delivering the key features. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should refine and adjust the Product Backlog to help the team focus on the highest value items in future Sprints. Changes to Sprint duration should not be made as they disrupt the team’s cadence. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Request the team to work overtime to meet the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: Asking the team to work overtime is not a sustainable or effective solution.
answer2: Adjust the Product Backlog priorities for the next Sprint to address delays.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting priorities helps the team focus on the most valuable work in upcoming Sprints.
answer3: Extend the current Sprint to allow more time to complete the work.
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprint durations are fixed and should not be extended.
answer4: Escalate the issue to management for immediate intervention.
explanation4: Incorrect: Escalating the issue is not the most effective way to address team delays.

title: Which two actions should a Product Owner take if stakeholders complain about the quality of the product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: To address quality concerns, the Product Owner should adjust the Product Backlog and incorporate quality measures into the Definition of Done. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Discuss the concerns with the Scrum Master to improve the team's approach.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master is not responsible for quality adjustments directly.
answer2: Adjust the Product Backlog to address quality issues in upcoming Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should refine the Backlog to improve the quality as per stakeholder feedback.
answer3: Reprimand the developers during the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reprimanding the team does not lead to constructive improvements.
answer4: Ensure quality standards are added to the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Correct: This approach makes sure that quality concerns are addressed in each Increment.
answer5: Increase the number of tests during the next Sprint.
explanation5: Incorrect: Testing alone does not directly address product quality improvement.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner's role in maximizing the value of the product? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes value by engaging with stakeholders, using data-driven decisions, and maintaining a well-refined Product Backlog that guides the team’s efforts. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delegating Backlog prioritization to the Scrum Master to streamline processes.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing the Backlog based on value and stakeholder input.
answer2: Regularly engaging stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures that the Product Backlog reflects current market needs and stakeholder expectations.
answer3: Using data and metrics to make informed prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help prioritize the most valuable work and align with business goals.
answer4: Ensuring Backlog items are refined and ready for future Sprints.
explanation4: Correct: A well-refined Backlog helps the team deliver consistent, incremental value.
answer5: Only focusing on high-priority items without considering stakeholder feedback.
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is essential for ensuring the Product Backlog aligns with business needs.

title: During the Sprint, a critical bug is discovered that affects the product’s core functionality. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the team to prioritize and address critical bugs within the current Sprint, maintaining product integrity and stakeholder trust. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the bug to maintain the Sprint focus.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring critical issues can lead to significant product failures and stakeholder dissatisfaction.
answer2: Work with the team to prioritize the bug fix within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Prioritizing critical bug fixes ensures the product remains functional and valuable.
answer3: Delay the fix until the next Sprint to avoid disrupting the current work.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying critical fixes compromises product quality and can create technical debt.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the bug independently.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should be involved in prioritizing issues, while the Scrum Master facilitates resolution.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Scrum Master's role in supporting the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the team by facilitating Scrum events, assisting the Product Owner with Backlog management, and coaching the team on self-management and collaboration. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Solving all technical issues for the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not directly solve technical challenges.
answer2: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive and effective.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating Scrum events is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer3: Helping the Product Owner manage the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the Product Owner in refining the Backlog and facilitating stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Coaching the team on self-management and cross-functionality.
explanation4: Correct: Coaching supports the team in becoming more self-sufficient and effective.
answer5: Directing the team’s daily work tasks.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not direct work; the team manages their own tasks.

title: Which artifact helps the Scrum Team track their progress toward completing the Sprint Goal and provides visibility into the team’s plan? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog provides a clear and transparent view of the team’s plan and progress during the Sprint, helping ensure alignment with the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists all future work but does not show progress within the current Sprint.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides transparency into the work planned and tracks progress during the Sprint.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment reflects completed work but does not track ongoing progress toward the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality standards but does not provide visibility into ongoing work.

title: Which artifact provides visibility into the work that has been completed and serves as a measure of progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment provides transparency into what has been completed and serves as evidence of progress toward the Product Goal. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog shows planned and future work but does not measure completed progress.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment reflects all completed work, providing a concrete measure of progress toward the Product Goal.
answer3: Sprint Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows the plan for the Sprint but does not reflect overall progress toward the Product Goal.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality standards but does not measure progress.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is required to set the Definition of Done for the Developers. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done is a commitment by the Scrum Team to ensure the work meets quality standards and is not the sole responsibility of the Product Owner. “The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a shared understanding created by the entire Scrum Team, not dictated by the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done is collectively defined by the Scrum Team, ensuring consistency in quality standards.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team finds that a critical Backlog item lacks sufficient details. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine the unclear item, ensuring it is clear and actionable before including it in the Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the item anyway to keep the Sprint on track.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including unclear items can disrupt the Sprint and reduce efficiency.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item immediately, ensuring it is ready and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement ensures the item is clear and can be effectively worked on during the Sprint.
answer3: Move the item to the next Sprint without refinement.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying refinement without addressing clarity can delay valuable work.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the refinement process.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner leads refinement with the Developers to ensure Backlog clarity.

title: What should the Product Owner do if they realize that the current Sprint Goal is no longer valuable? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If the Sprint Goal loses its value, the Product Owner has the responsibility to cancel the Sprint and redirect the team's focus. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Cancel the Sprint and start planning a new one.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint if the goal becomes obsolete.
answer2: Continue with the current Sprint as planned to maintain team morale.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Sprint should only continue if the goal remains valuable.
answer3: Discuss with the Developers about changing the goal mid-Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal should remain consistent once the Sprint has started.
answer4: Consult with the Scrum Master to adjust the current Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjusting the Sprint is not a suitable response when the goal is no longer valuable.

title: Which three key factors should be considered when creating a Definition of Done? (Choose the three best answers)
