feedback: The Definition of Done ensures quality by incorporating team-agreed standards, compliance requirements, and stakeholder expectations, guiding the team’s work. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Quality criteria agreed upon by the entire Scrum Team.
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done reflects shared standards that ensure quality and consistency.
answer2: Compliance with organizational and industry standards.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done should incorporate relevant compliance and regulatory requirements.
answer3: Stakeholder expectations for the final product.
explanation3: Correct: Including stakeholder expectations helps ensure that the Increment meets end-user needs and is valuable.
answer4: Speed of task completion during the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done focuses on quality, not the speed of task completion.
answer5: Personal preferences of the team members.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a collective agreement, not based on individual preferences.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner’s role in ensuring the Product Backlog is effectively managed? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Product Backlog management involves continuous refinement, stakeholder engagement, and data-driven prioritization to maintain alignment with business goals. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delegating Product Backlog management entirely to the Developers.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner must actively manage the Product Backlog to ensure alignment with product goals.
answer2: Engaging with stakeholders to refine and prioritize items based on feedback and value.
explanation2: Correct: Engaging with stakeholders ensures the Product Backlog reflects current needs and priorities.
answer3: Using data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help keep the Product Backlog focused on delivering maximum value.
answer4: Ensuring items are refined, clear, and ready for selection in future Sprints.
explanation4: Correct: A well-refined Backlog facilitates smoother Sprint Planning and helps the team deliver consistent value.
answer5: Updating the Backlog only during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning.
explanation5: Incorrect: Product Backlog refinement is a continuous process, not limited to formal events.

title: Which two strategies should the Product Owner use to ensure that the Product Backlog reflects current market needs? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should regularly engage with stakeholders and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with current market needs and value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only update the Product Backlog during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously updated based on new insights, not just during formal events.
answer2: Engage regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement ensures the Product Backlog stays relevant and aligned with market conditions.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help keep the Product Backlog focused on the most impactful work.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to maintain the Backlog’s current structure.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Backlog adaptable and responsive to changes.
answer5: Delegate Backlog updates to the Developers to streamline the process.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for managing the Product Backlog and cannot delegate this responsibility.

title: Which two actions are recommended if the team consistently fails to meet the Sprint Goal? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Facilitating Retrospectives to identify root causes and coaching the team on setting realistic Sprint Goals are effective strategies to help the team meet their objectives consistently. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Facilitate a Sprint Retrospective to identify root causes and plan improvements.
explanation1: Correct: The Retrospective allows the team to reflect on failures and make actionable plans to avoid repeating mistakes.
answer2: Coach the team on setting realistic Sprint Goals during Sprint Planning.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master can guide the team to set achievable goals, aligning expectations with capacity.
answer3: Extend the Sprint duration to provide more time to meet the goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint duration disrupts the cadence and undermines Scrum principles.
answer4: Reassign tasks to more skilled team members.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reassigning tasks disrupts team dynamics and undermines self-organization.
answer5: Report the issue to management for guidance.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Team is self-managing and responsible for addressing its own issues internally.

title: The Product Owner frequently changes the priorities of Product Backlog items mid-Sprint, causing confusion. How should the Development Team respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Discussing priority changes during the Sprint Retrospective helps the team and Product Owner align on a consistent approach, improving collaboration and focus. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity to improve quality and effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Accept the changes to keep the Product Owner satisfied.
explanation1: Incorrect: Accepting changes mid-Sprint can disrupt the team’s focus and undermine their commitment to the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Discuss the impact of changes with the Product Owner during the Sprint Retrospective to find a better approach.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective is an appropriate setting to address recurring issues and agree on how to handle priority changes in future Sprints.
answer3: Ignore the changes and continue with the original plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback from the Product Owner can cause misalignment and damage collaboration.
answer4: Reprioritize tasks as soon as the Product Owner requests changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reprioritizing without discussion can lead to chaos and undermine the Sprint Goal.

title: The Scrum Master notices that the Daily Scrum meetings are frequently exceeding 15 minutes. What is the best course of action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master’s role is to ensure that the Daily Scrum remains within the 15-minute time-box, coaching the team to be concise and focused. “The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and is kept within the time-box.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Encourage the team to stick strictly to the time limit and only discuss key points.
explanation1: Correct: The Scrum Master should coach the team to focus on essential points and adhere to the time-box to maintain the effectiveness of the Daily Scrum.
answer2: Extend the meeting time to allow the team to discuss all issues in detail.
explanation2: Incorrect: Extending the meeting undermines the purpose of the time-box and can lead to inefficiency.
answer3: Remove the Daily Scrum and replace it with one-on-one check-ins.
explanation3: Incorrect: Removing the Daily Scrum removes the team’s opportunity to inspect and adapt together.
answer4: Schedule an additional meeting to discuss the issues in detail.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adding more meetings disrupts team flow and does not address the root problem of staying focused.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders express dissatisfaction with the Increment delivered. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is an opportunity for stakeholders to provide feedback that should be captured and used to adjust the Product Backlog, informing future work. “The Scrum Team and stakeholders collaborate on what to do next, so that the Sprint Review provides valuable input to subsequent Sprint Planning.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Rework the Increment immediately to address the stakeholders’ concerns.
explanation1: Incorrect: Reworking during the Sprint Review is not appropriate; feedback should inform future Sprints.
answer2: Capture feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Feedback from the Sprint Review should be used to refine the Product Backlog and improve future work.
answer3: Extend the Sprint to address the concerns raised.
explanation3: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint disrupts the time-box and is not allowed in Scrum.
answer4: Request that the Scrum Master handle stakeholder concerns.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Team should collectively address feedback, not defer it solely to the Scrum Master.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must approve every Increment before it is considered Done. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers ensure that each Increment meets the Definition of Done, and it is considered complete without the need for additional approval. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not approve Increments; they are considered Done when they meet the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: An Increment is considered Done when it meets the Scrum Team’s Definition of Done, not upon approval by the Product Owner.

title: During the Sprint, a key stakeholder insists on adding a high-priority item. How should the Product Owner handle this request? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate the stakeholder’s request and manage it through the Product Backlog, ensuring that changes do not disrupt the ongoing Sprint. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Add the item to the current Sprint Backlog to satisfy the stakeholder.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding items to the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint disrupts the focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the item and prioritize it in the Product Backlog for future consideration.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should evaluate the item and manage it through the Product Backlog, not disrupt the ongoing Sprint.
answer3: Ignore the request to maintain the current Sprint scope.
explanation3: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback should be acknowledged, not ignored.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to communicate the refusal to the stakeholder.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.
